clauses.reason: Executive Order 11408, signed 1968-04-25 (33 FR 6459, printed 1968-04-27), revokes in section 1 Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (dual Federal-State office holding) and Executive Order No. 9367 of August 4, 1943 (prohibiting Government employees from instructing persons for certain Government examinations), and in section 2 all prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9, naming a list of numbers. Both commands are one-time revocations performed when the order takes effect. The order has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, 1968-04-25 (the printing date 1968-04-27 is an alternative reading, not an end; the day number in the held signature line is garbled, and the date rests on the census register, the Office of the Federal Register catalog and the filing line of April 25, 1968). The clause is exhausted by performance on that date (owner ruling 2026-10-28: a used one-time command is recorded as exhausted by performance, separate from any surviving consequence; the surviving consequence here is the revoked status of the named orders, which is not a command of this order). The cited source is the order's own held text, which contains the words are hereby revoked in both sections. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11408 (33 FR 6459, Federal Register of April 27, 1968; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 11408, Revoking Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, and amendatory orders, relating to dual Federal-State office holding, and Executive Order No. 9367 of August 4, 1943, signed by Lyndon B. Johnson; the census register and the Office of the Federal Register catalog give the signing date 1968-04-25, and the held text shows filing on April 25, 1968 (the day number in the signature line is garbled in the text layer). Inventory: section 1 revokes Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 and Executive Order No. 9367 of August 4, 1943; section 2 revokes all prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9, naming a list of numbers that begins with 9-2 of January 28, 1873 and ends with 10645 of November 22, 1955. The dossier's single whole-order clause covers both sections and matches. Lifecycle: both commands are one-time revocations performed when the order took effect. The order has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, 1968-04-25; the printing date 1968-04-27 is an alternative reading, not an end. The clause is exhausted by performance on 1968-04-25. Dossier missing item (target provision not located, EO 11222): EO 11222 is not a target of this order; it is a cross-reference in the Office of the Federal Register editorial note on this order, which says see EO 11222 with the date May 8, 1968 although EO 11222 was signed on 1965-05-08; an order signed in 1965 cannot be a later event of this 1968 order, and nothing in this order's text names it. It is not relied on. Searches: the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches record no later instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes this order (the catalog's two hits are editorial cross-references, one to EO 11222 and one to 5 U.S.C. 7301 and section 735.203 of the Civil Service regulations, as described); a held-corpus search by number returns only this order's own printings; the order is not in the table of EO 12553.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording; the held text was read in full. The revocations were complete on 1968-04-25; what the revoked orders prescribed before that date was an effect of those orders, not a command of this one. Nothing in the held evidence shows a continuing right or duty arising from this order.
